title: A Parser as a Higher-Order Function: char(c)
description: Build the foundational char(c) parser that takes a character c and returns a function parse(s, pos) -> (value, next_pos) | None.

steps.description: Define char(c), which returns an inner function parse(s, pos) that checks pos < len(s) and s[pos] == c.
When s[pos] matches c, parse returns the tuple (c, pos + 1); otherwise it returns None without consuming any input.

steps.question: What do p('abc', 0) and p('abc', 1) return when p = char('a')?
steps.answer: At pos 0, s[0] is 'a', so p('abc', 0) returns ('a', 1); at pos 1, s[1] is 'b', so p('abc', 1) returns None.

steps.description: Create p = char('a') and test it on ('abc', 0), ('abc', 1), and ('', 0).
Watch parse('abc', 0) match 'a' at index 0 and return ('a', 1).
